findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a repo adopted with Actions before this fix has `test_place = "ci"` and `checks = ["forge-pr-check"]`.
The owner-approved Done-when is: Adopting an app with GitHub Actions writes checks with tests and forge-pr-check like a new repo, and forge doctor tells an existing repo whose checks name only forge-pr-check the exact checks line that moves its tests to CI.
New evidence beyond the coordinator's local-fallback ruling: the raw-parent adoption code writes this explicit CI setting for `--actions yes --checks forge-pr-check`. `src/forge/prcheck.py:252` and `:370` omit the PR tests job without a `tests` check, while `src/forge/close.py:246` leaves tests to CI. This guard suppresses the repair advice, so subsequent PRs receive no app-test run even though the repo selected CI. Adding the `tests` check can preserve that explicit choice.

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an existing Actions job runs app integration tests against a PostgreSQL service container and supplies its connection settings in that job.
Adding `tests` makes Forge generate and wait for a separate required job. The job in `src/forge/prcheck.py:81` through `:110` does not carry over the existing job's service or environment; GitHub scopes service containers to their own job ([GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/use-containerized-services/use-docker-service-containers)). For an adopted app whose `npm ci && npm test` needs that database, the existing check passes but Forge's new check fails, blocking adoption and later changes.
findings.title: Preserve existing CI service setup when requiring the new tests check

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4 (floor: migration)
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an earlier-adopted repo follows the warning while its default branch has Forge's normal branch protection.
Adds work: reconcile the required GitHub checks after the repair; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4.
New evidence beyond the coordinator's warning-only ruling: `forge sync` writes generated files but does not update branch protection (`src/forge/sync.py:684`), and `src/forge/close.py:187` updates protection only for an adoption or migration. After the suggested fix merges, GitHub still requires only `forge-pr-check`; the new `tests` check is not enforced by branch protection, and doctor reports a checks mismatch at `src/forge/doctor.py:465`. Forge's close waits for tests, but GitHub's protection does not require them to pass ([GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)).
findings.title: Reconcile branch protection when applying the doctor's checks repair

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - an earlier adoption explicitly chooses to run tests locally.
The fixture ends inside `[models.review]` (`tests/fixtures/adopted-v1.2.2/client/forge.toml:41`), so appending `test_place = "local"` here puts it in that table, not at the TOML root. `src/forge/repo.py:913` rejects the resulting model setting before doctor reaches the new warning. The negative assertion still passes because it does not establish that doctor reached the valid explicit-local case, so this named proof cannot detect an incorrect warning for that choice.

why: An app adopted into Forge with GitHub Actions gets checks = forge-pr-check only, so Forge's tests job never runs the changed tests in CI and an earlier-adopted repo without test_place falls back to running every close's tests on the laptop
